It improves multiple reasoning and assistant tasks while maintaining competitive inference cost, but the abstract gives no exact cost or latency reduction, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: From Concentration to Differentiation and Back: Routing Effective Rank in MoE Reasoning Cohorts
historical_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / efficient reasoning / routing characterization
historical_watchlist.why: Introduces routing effective rank as a label-free measure of cross-rollout MoE expert-routing organization during test-time scaling, with a reproducible low-high-low trajectory across ten MoE configurations and five reasoning benchmarks. This is useful systems characterization for dynamic routing and test-time compute policies, but it does not itself provide a serving speedup, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Temporal Tactile Encoding and Compliance for Intent-Aware Robot-to-Human Bimanual Handover
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / multimodal VLA / tactile control
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work coupling a VLA model with temporal tactile encoding, proprioception, and a compliance controller for intent-aware bimanual handover. Human-subject evaluation shows complementary gains over visual-only and tactile-without-compliance baselines, but no measured inference latency or compute reduction is reported, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: TourPhysics: Bringing Physics to World Models for Exploration and Manipulation from a Single Image
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world models / physics-grounded generation
historical_watchlist.why: Protected world-model work that couples deterministic simulation, geometric evidence, generator controls, and persistent appearance memory for online exploration and manipulation from a single image. It improves trajectory adherence and long-horizon revisit consistency over baselines, but does not report serving/runtime acceleration metrics, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Toward Sustainable Distributed LLM Inference: A Systems Synthesis and Research Agenda for an Energy-, Carbon-, and Cache-Aware llm-d Control Plane
historical_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / distributed inference / cache-aware scheduling / sustainable systems
historical_watchlist.why: Systems synthesis connecting model/phase/cache/hardware/replica/region/time decisions for distributed LLM inference and proposing an energy-, carbon-, and cache-aware llm-d control plane with SLO-satisfied goodput-per-joule and per-CO2e evaluation. It explicitly states that its contribution is synthesis rather than new benchmark results, so it is retained as a high-value systems agenda watch rather than promoted strong.

historical_watchlist.title: RoboCousin: Build Your Own Simulation Playground for Robust Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / synthetic data systems / bimanual manipulation
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI data-system work that converts user observations into simulation-ready assets, scenes, grasp-contact annotations and expert trajectories. RoboCousin-OBD contains over 3,000 object instances and 50 environments, and the pipeline generates over one million trajectories across 50 tasks with sim-to-real validation. It improves data scalability rather than inference latency, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Towards Neuro-Symbolic Procedural Reasoning for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Manipulation
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / long-horizon VLA / procedural memory
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work combining learned VLA control with explicit task graphs and multimodal procedural memory to maintain long-horizon task state, dependencies, conditional branches and visual evidence. It is an ECCV 2026 workshop extended abstract and does not report compute-side speedup, so it is retained as a high-value watch for VLA runtime/state architecture rather than promoted strong.

historical_watchlist.title: Query-Aware Token Budgeting for Efficient Late-Interaction Visual Document Retrieval
historical_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / retrieval systems / token compression
historical_watchlist.why: Uses a heavily compressed hot-path index followed by query-aware stage-two token budgeting over shortlisted pages, recovering 98.39% of full-token score with greedy marginal-gain selection under a pool-factor-eight-equivalent reranking budget. The latency analysis identifies practical operating points but the abstract gives no direct end-to-end speedup, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: NOVA-CIM: Noise- and Correlation-Tolerant Stochastic Interfaces for Analog Compute-in-Memory
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / compute-in-memory / accelerator interfaces
historical_watchlist.why: Replaces multi-bit ADC readout with random-reference 1-bit sensing and lightweight stochastic counting for analog CIM, targeting energy-efficient inference while improving robustness to read noise and correlated stochastic inputs. End-to-end ViT-Base accuracy remains 84.48% versus 84.51% BF16 under modeled read noise, but no measured latency/energy speedup is reported, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: KVShareArena: KV-Cache Reuse Across Contexts and Model Checkpoints
historical_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / LLM serving / benchmark and cost accounting
historical_watchlist.why: KVShareArena benchmarks non-prefix KV-cache reuse across retrieved chunks, multi-agent reports and model checkpoints, explicitly charging compute, memory and per-request latency and separating one-time cache-build cost. It shows position correction is often enough for single-source reuse but multi-source reuse needs partial re-encoding or training, and unrepaired caches can be worse than no cache. High-value systems benchmark, but not itself a new acceleration runtime.

historical_watchlist.title: TRACE: Trajectory-robust Admission with Evidence Ordering for Efficient GUI Agents
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / multimodal serving / KV cache / token pruning
historical_watchlist.why: TRACE addresses irreversible visual-token admission in long GUI-agent trajectories with query-independent interaction priors, instruction relevance, novelty and coverage repair, plus monotone KV contraction to avoid repeated visual encoding or pruning. It is directly relevant to agent memory/serving efficiency across six GUI benchmarks, but the primary abstract provides no exact latency, memory or throughput reduction, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: SymbolicLight V2: Hybrid Neuromorphic Architecture and Sparse Execution for Low-Energy Language Inference
historical_watchlist.why: Hybrid neuromorphic language architecture implemented on Alveo U50C and ARM. Same-checkpoint FPGA variants raise decode throughput from 474.6 to 643.2 tok/s and cut gross card energy/token 27.6%; however the deployed checkpoint trails a same-budget dense control in quality, so the paper does not establish equal-quality efficiency and remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
historical_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / efficient reasoning / agent memory
historical_watchlist.why: Training-free hierarchical-convolution memory shortens sequential segment processing to a logarithmic tree and exposes parallelism across text segments and reasoning threads. It improves RULER HotpotQA/2WikiMultiHopQA over training-free baselines, but the primary evidence gives no measured latency, throughput, or token-cost reduction, so it stays high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: PASCAL: A Phase-Aware Shared-Cache Model for Parallel Scans
historical_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / cache modeling / AI accelerators
historical_watchlist.why: Models progress divergence across multicore parallel scans such as attention K/V reuse and GEMM panel reuse without requiring target traces or cycle timing. On 60 NVIDIA GB10 configurations it reaches 13.84% MAPE versus 44.79% for TileSight and 54.16% for exact symbolic SDCM. Valuable design-space model, but not itself an acceleration mechanism.

historical_watchlist.title: Frequency-Conditioned Flow Matching for Vision-Language-Action Models
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / flow matching / action generation
historical_watchlist.why: FreqFM makes action frequency an explicit conditioning dimension for flow-matching VLA action experts using DCT-space source matching, frequency-balanced objectives, and frequency-scaled guidance. It improves LIBERO-Plus by 9.3 points and also validates on six real-robot tasks, but reports algorithmic task gains rather than serving/runtime efficiency, so it is retained as protected Physical-AI watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Distribution-Consistent Inference for Dynamic Sparse Mixture-of-Experts
historical_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / dynamic routing / sparse inference
historical_watchlist.why: Findings EMNLP 2026 identifies representation-scale shift when inference-time top-k is reduced and proposes lightweight layer-wise distribution alignment using calibration statistics. It recovers much of the lost quality while preserving dynamic sparse-routing efficiency with negligible overhead, but the primary abstract gives no concrete latency/FLOP/throughput reduction, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: DiffLUT-Net: Differentiable Training of FPGA LUT Networks with Learnable Connectivity
historical_watchlist.why: FPGA-native networks jointly learn six-input LUT truth tables and sparse connectivity, then export directly to synthesizable Verilog and prune unused logic. It reports favorable accuracy-resource tradeoffs across five benchmarks and releases code, but the abstract provides no exact latency/energy/throughput advantage, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Safe Task Planning with Long-Term Graph Memory for Embodied Agents
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / embodied agents / long-term memory / safety
historical_watchlist.why: CoRL 2026 SafeMem maintains a long-term semantic graph under partial observability and uses an LLM risk predictor plus conservatism-modulated replanning. It substantially improves safe success on IS-Bench and a real robot platform, making it a protected Physical-AI memory/safety node, but it reports no serving or compute-efficiency metric.

historical_watchlist.title: Show-Harness: Just a VLM Agent Can Play Robots
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / VLM agents / robot interface / low-cost deployment
historical_watchlist.why: Show-Harness exposes compact semantic action units with embodiment-specific deterministic interpreters, allowing frontier VLMs to control robots zero-shot and small open VLMs to adapt with only a few GPU-hours. It generalizes across tasks and embodiments without added model capacity or costly embodiment-specific pretraining, but lacks direct serving latency/throughput measurements, so it remains protected Physical-AI watch.

historical_watchlist.title: DFlow: Enabling Verifier Information Flow in Block Diffusion Speculative Decoding
historical_watchlist.topic: speculative decoding / diffusion language models / verifier reuse
historical_watchlist.why: DFlow reuses verifier hidden states from rejected suffix positions across drafting rounds, so spent verifier computation informs later drafts without extra target computation, and self-conditioning teaches that cross-round information flow. It improves draft quality and acceptance length over DFlash on Qwen3, but the primary abstract gives no exact end-to-end throughput or latency speedup, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Accuracy is Not Enough: A Divergence-Based Approach to Evaluate Fidelity Loss in Quantized LLMs
historical_watchlist.why: A 120-run matrix across five foundation architectures and four reasoning benchmarks evaluates progressive quantization from BF16 to Q2_K using full-vocabulary JS/TV divergence rather than only argmax accuracy. It shows mixed-precision Q4_K generally preserves distribution fidelity better than Q4_0 at similar memory footprints. This is a useful deployment-quality diagnostic rather than a new acceleration method, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: LIBERO-RECOVER: Beyond Task Success Towards Failure Recovery in Robotic Manipulation Models
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / evaluation / failure recovery / robustness
historical_watchlist.why: Introduces 1,000+ real execution-failure scenarios on LIBERO across action retry, adaptation, object-state recovery, and environmental recovery, explicitly targeting VLA/WAM deployment robustness beyond nominal task success. It is a protected Physical-AI benchmark rather than a compute/serving acceleration paper, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Hi-FLoop: Hierarchical State-Feedback Loops for Multi-Timescale World Modeling
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / world models / multi-timescale closed-loop generation
historical_watchlist.why: Hierarchical branch-consistent traffic world model separates 8-s Goal, 2-s Preview, 1-s Control, and 0.5-s feedback commits, with sparse future interaction graphs and generated-state recovery. It directly matches multi-timescale Physical-AI system structure, but currently reports predictive quality rather than serving/runtime savings, so it remains protected watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Proxy Policy Steering
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / inference-time adaptation / flow policy steering
historical_watchlist.why: Inference-time adaptation trains lightweight reference and task proxy policies whose velocity-space residual steers a frozen generalist sampler at every denoising step. Across 8 real and 4 simulation manipulation tasks it improves pi-0.5 by 53% absolute success on average while retaining broad base capabilities; strong Physical-AI relevance, but no measured serving latency/compute reduction in the primary abstract.

historical_watchlist.title: RefGuard: Identity-Aware Language-Guided Robot Manipulation via Joint Target-Anchor-Frame Grounding
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / deployment reliability / grounding / robot runtime
historical_watchlist.why: Maintains a joint target-anchor-reference-frame posterior and defers execution when grounding is ambiguous. On a real UF850 arm it records zero identity switches on ambiguity-stress trials and 90.0% correct execution versus 33-46% identity-switch rates for baselines; protected deployment-reliability work rather than a compute acceleration method.

historical_watchlist.title: Why Is Video Still So Expensive? A Survey of Inference-Efficiency Mechanisms in Video and Audiovisual LLMs
historical_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / video inference / efficiency survey / canonical lineage
historical_watchlist.why: Recent survey focused specifically on VideoLLM inference-efficiency mechanisms with concrete parameter, FLOP, latency, memory, visual-token, or audio-token reductions. Useful as a canonical map and recall seed across token pruning, temporal sampling, caching, compression, and multimodal serving, but it is a survey rather than a new acceleration method.

historical_watchlist.title: GIFT: Guided Intermediate Feature Training via Action-Oriented Structural Supervision for Robotic Manipulation
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / representation learning / action-oriented structure
historical_watchlist.why: Architecture-flexible structural supervision preserves geometry, affordance, and goal information in intermediate features across VLA, direct-action WAM, and inverse-dynamics WAM. On LIBERO-Plus the three variants reach 79.6%, 72.6%, and 87.8%, and on RoboCasa 61.4%, 83.6%, and 82.3%; important protected Physical-AI work but not a measured inference-speed method.

historical_watchlist.title: Where Success Breaks: Failure-Boundary Learning for Robust Vision-Language-Action Models
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / robust adaptation / failure recovery
historical_watchlist.why: Frames robust VLA adaptation as discovering, localizing, and shaping failure boundaries rather than only fitting successful demonstrations. DLS uses real-grounded priors plus simulated co-training to expose recovery boundaries; retained as a protected deployment-robustness watch item because the main contribution is reliability rather than measured serving efficiency.

historical_watchlist.title: Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Sample-Adaptive Strategy Routing for Vision Token Pruning in MLLMs
historical_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / vision token pruning / adaptive routing
historical_watchlist.why: VIP-Router selects among pruning strategies per input with only 0.017% trainable backbone-equivalent parameters. It improves average accuracy by 26.9% relative and utility accounting for realized token cost by 22.0% versus the best fixed strategy, but the abstract does not report end-to-end latency or throughput.

historical_watchlist.title: Programmable World Model
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / world models / persistent state / programmable simulation
historical_watchlist.why: Decouples explicit persistent world-state evolution from video rendering through executable programs and state-augmented 3D OBB conditioning. CombatStateBench reports 94% Count Accuracy and 98% State Accuracy; retained as a protected WAM systems item because the contribution is world-state architecture rather than measured inference acceleration.

historical_watchlist.title: EnvCraft: Synthesizing Executable Environments in Agentic RL for Claw-like Agent
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / agentic RL / executable environments / training infrastructure
historical_watchlist.why: Automates sandboxed executable-environment synthesis and topology-aware task generation, producing 139 environments and about 20K complex tasks. Qwen3/3.5 8B-32B models gain up to 11.9% on Claw benchmarks and 8.0% on tool-use benchmarks with reduced inference token cost, but the abstract does not quantify the cost reduction.

historical_watchlist.title: Scaling Post-Training Ternarisation to Qwen3-8B Capability Retention, Reproduction, Lossless Packing, and Packed Execution
historical_watchlist.topic: quantization / ultra-low-bit LLM / packed execution / deployment characterization
historical_watchlist.why: Provides an end-to-end Qwen3-8B ternarisation and deployment characterization including lossless packing and direct packed execution at 15.52 tokens/s in 7.35 GiB. It is valuable negative/engineering evidence because the preliminary packed GEMV is still slower than FP16 cuBLAS, so it is retained as watch rather than promoted as an acceleration result.

historical_watchlist.title: From Fixed Keys to Readable Schemas: Small Language Models for Vehicle Agent Function Calls
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / edge agents / on-device SLM / function calling
historical_watchlist.why: Benchmarks Functional Tokens versus Schema-in-Prompt for 270M-1.7B on-device vehicle agents across 9,822 examples and 79 Android Automotive functions, explicitly exposing the compact-inference versus unseen-function-generalization tradeoff. Important protected edge-Physical-AI evidence, but no exact latency or memory numbers are reported in the abstract.

historical_watchlist.title: Communication-Efficient Personalized Federated Learning via Layer-Wise Multi-Threshold Random Sketching
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / federated learning / communication compression / low-bit sketching
historical_watchlist.why: Uses layer-specific multi-threshold random sketches for bidirectional personalized federated learning communication, improving the communication-accuracy tradeoff over one-bit compression baselines. The primary abstract does not report an exact byte, bandwidth, latency, or round reduction, so it is retained as a high-value systems watch rather than promoted strong.

historical_watchlist.title: Steering Under Compression: Dose-Response, Capability Cost, and Failure Asymmetry in Quantized LLMs
historical_watchlist.topic: quantization / LLM deployment / activation steering / capability-cost characterization
historical_watchlist.why: Systematically studies inference-time activation steering under INT8 and NF4 across four open 7-9B models. It finds steering directions largely survive compression but capability-cost and failure behavior change substantially, including a Mistral-NF4 GSM8K baseline shift from 0.545 to 0.365. Valuable deployment characterization, but not a new acceleration method.

historical_watchlist.title: BIFTA: Brain-Inspired Few-Shot Tactile Adaptation for Unknown Sensors
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / tactile sensing / few-shot adaptation / heterogeneous sensors
historical_watchlist.why: Adapts a frozen tactile encoder to previously unseen sensor hardware using a small labeled support set, dual-view statistical memory, spectral graphs, and uncertainty-gated propagation. With 10% labeled target data on SITR, mean Sparsh accuracy rises from 6.86% to 87.09%, but this is data-efficient adaptation rather than measured inference acceleration.

historical_watchlist.title: FolDeX: A Physical-World Benchmark for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation of Deformable Objects
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / long-horizon manipulation / deformable objects / real-robot benchmark
historical_watchlist.why: Introduces a real-robot benchmark for long-horizon deformable manipulation with 2,000+ hours of physical data, 20+ tasks, and 10+ embodiments, explicitly studying reuse of intervention, recovery, cross-task, cross-scene, and cross-embodiment experience. It is a high-value Physical-AI evaluation and data-reuse resource, not an inference acceleration method.

historical_watchlist.title: CEDD-optimizer: Enabling Cost-Efficient Dataset Distillation on Geographically Distributed Edge Systems
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / distributed dataset distillation / cost optimization
historical_watchlist.why: Optimizes dataset-distillation compression ratio and distillation steps across geographically distributed edge devices under heterogeneous energy and transfer prices. The abstract reports up to a 20.8 improvement over baseline under the same quality constraint, but the unit is not explicit in the primary abstract, so it is retained as high-value watch rather than promoted strong.

historical_watchlist.title: Protocol Compression Changes Which Party Pays: Bilateral Cost in Cross-Organization LLM Agent Communication
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / agent communication / protocol compression / token cost
historical_watchlist.why: Measures bilateral token and monetary cost of compressed protocols across six vendors and 1,053 completed cross-organization agent dialogues. Negotiated sessions cost 52% of the English baseline largely because they terminate sooner, while break-even horizons are 20-70 turns and some vendor pairs reverse which endpoint is cheaper. Valuable deployment economics and communication-efficiency evidence, but not a generally positive acceleration method.

historical_watchlist.title: MEMO: Multimodal Evidence Memory Organization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / long-horizon memory / multimodal evidence budgeting
historical_watchlist.why: Selects relevant evidence blocks and assigns them to textual, visual, or dual-channel carriers under a constrained working-memory budget. Across HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, LoCoMo, and ALFWorld it reports fewer memory tokens with improved downstream performance, but the primary abstract gives no exact latency, token-reduction, or cost ratio, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: SIDE: Sensor Impersonation Detection at the Edge via Sequence Prediction
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / edge inference / quantization / tiny ML
historical_watchlist.why: Deploys an LSTM detector on Arduino Nano 33 BLE and compares non-quantized, 16-bit, and 8-bit variants: model size falls from 554 KB to 298.5 KB and 185 KB, while the authors explicitly report quantization made execution slower in their measurements. This is a useful hardware-aware negative result for edge quantization, not a strong acceleration result.

historical_watchlist.title: GTA-2: A Multi-VLM Framework for Synthesizing Robot Manipulation Skills via Grounded Task Axes
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / multi-VLM skill synthesis / zero-shot manipulation / modular control
historical_watchlist.why: Factorizes manipulation into semantic subtasks, grounded task axes, controller parameters, and visual grounding using four specialized VLM agents, enabling zero-shot executable skill synthesis without robot demonstrations or task-specific fine-tuning. On 14 real-robot tasks it reaches 73.9% zero-shot success versus the strongest baseline by +31.4 points, rising to 90.7% with targeted refinement; this is high-value Physical-AI architecture evidence but not measured inference acceleration.

historical_watchlist.title: Encrypt What Matters: When Selective Homomorphic Inference Is Efficient
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / privacy-preserving inference / selective FHE
historical_watchlist.why: Shows that encrypting only sensitive ROIs can preserve exact outputs while locality-preserving architectures obtain order-of-magnitude homomorphic-evaluation speedups, whereas early global mixing removes the benefit. This is valuable architectural efficiency evidence, but the abstract presents conditional rather than a single deployment-wide benchmark, so it is retained as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Efficient Multi-Timescale Event Representations for Feed-Forward Object Detection
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / event perception / feed-forward detection / neuromorphic efficiency
historical_watchlist.why: Encodes multi-timescale temporal information directly in event representations and introduces a recursive approximation for efficient event-by-event updates, reducing reliance on recurrent temporal modeling while preserving detection performance. The primary abstract does not quantify latency, throughput, or energy gains, so it remains a protected Physical-AI watch item.

historical_watchlist.title: Compact Neural Appearance Models for Efficient Gaussian Splatting
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / 3DGS / compact appearance representation / CUDA rendering
historical_watchlist.why: Performs an end-to-end comparison of spherical-harmonic and learned spherical appearance models inside one optimized differentiable CUDA rasterizer, and introduces compact per-primitive latent codes decoded by a tiny shared MLP. The representation directly targets per-primitive storage and memory traffic and includes rendering-performance evaluation, but the primary abstract does not expose a single quantitative speedup or memory-reduction figure, so it remains a protected high-value watch item.

historical_watchlist.title: Open-Set 3D Scene Graphs for Field Robotics: An Outdoor Case Study
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / scene graph memory / field robotics / open-set VLM mapping
historical_watchlist.why: Systematically evaluates semantic embeddings, graph navigation, region understanding and memory size of an open-set 3D scene graph across five outdoor robotic datasets, including repeated-traversal consistency. It is valuable evidence for persistent spatial memory and VLM-grounded world-state infrastructure, but it is a characterization study rather than a measured inference-acceleration method.

historical_watchlist.title: NutriBench-Kitchen: Benchmarking Embodied AI for Nutrition Management
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / persistent embodied memory / long-horizon kitchen agents
historical_watchlist.why: Introduces 1,500 manually verified QA pairs from 160 cooking videos covering ingredient entry, memory management, recipe query and long/short-term planning, explicitly testing whether embodied agents continuously maintain and use persistent food state. It fills a useful long-horizon memory benchmark gap but does not present serving or runtime-efficiency gains, so it is retained only as protected Physical-AI watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Agentic ML Exploration (A-MLE) for Ads Ranking
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / ML infrastructure / autonomous experimentation / industrial ranking
historical_watchlist.why: Industrial autonomous ML-exploration system deployed across a portfolio of large-scale ads-ranking models, coordinating hypothesis generation, experiment execution, analysis and shared knowledge with sandboxed tools and human checkpoints. It directly targets the human-throughput bottleneck of ML iteration, but the primary abstract does not expose a clean quantitative latency, compute, or cost reduction, so it remains high-value watch rather than strong.

historical_watchlist.title: ReactVAU: A Slow-Fast Decoupled Framework for Streaming Video Anomaly Understanding
historical_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / streaming video / conditional MLLM invocation / persistent memory
historical_watchlist.why: Introduces a slow-fast streaming design where a lightweight detector continuously filters the stream, anomaly-aware persistent memory preserves rare events, and heavyweight MLLM reasoning wakes only on suspicious events. The paper explicitly reports substantially fewer heavyweight MLLM invocations and real-time streaming operation, but the primary abstract omits a single quantitative latency/throughput figure, so it is retained as a high-value serving watch item.

historical_watchlist.title: Compact Bellman-Grounded Cognitive Maps for Cost-Aware Navigation
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / navigation memory / compact world representation / cost-aware planning
historical_watchlist.why: Learns a reusable Bellman-grounded cognitive map with compact coordinate encoding, enabling changing navigation goals without per-goal retraining. On grids up to 1,600 nodes it maintains full success with only 5% mean gap to Dijkstra, while memory growth is sublinear from 400 to 3,600 nodes. It is valuable protected evidence for compact embodied memory, but not a direct VLA/WAM inference accelerator.

historical_watchlist.title: One Diffusion Model, Two Roles: Guided Trajectory Planning and Safety-Critical Scenario Generation in Closed-Loop Simulation
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / autonomous driving / diffusion planning / closed-loop simulation
historical_watchlist.why: Uses one pretrained diffusion traffic model both as an ego planner and as a controllable safety-critical scenario generator, with training-free clean-sample guidance that avoids auxiliary networks. This is highly relevant to WAM/world-model and action-planning lineage, but the abstract emphasizes closed-loop quality and controllability rather than measured inference acceleration, so it remains protected watch.

historical_watchlist.title: PLSR: Progressive and Localized Super-Resolution of 3D Objects via Localized Latent Voxel Diffusion
historical_watchlist.topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / 3D generation / localized denoising / memory efficiency
historical_watchlist.why: Decomposes global 3D super-resolution into localized latent-voxel diffusion subproblems with low-cost finetuning and patch-wise denoising, explicitly targeting memory and computational efficiency for high-resolution 3D generation. The primary abstract claims significant computational-cost reduction but gives no exact speedup or memory number, so it is kept as a high-value diffusion-efficiency watch item.

historical_watchlist.title: QPS-ToR: A Parallel Iterative Switching Algorithm for Reconfigurable Optical Datacenter Switching
historical_watchlist.topic: distributed training/inference / datacenter networking / optical switching / low-complexity scheduling
historical_watchlist.why: Replaces single-iteration iSLIP in a reconfigurable optical datacenter fabric with sliding-window QPS and, in 128-ToR flow simulations, reports up to 36% higher throughput and 82% lower flow completion time versus NegotiaToR. The system result is strong, but the current paper is workload-agnostic rather than AI-specific, so it is retained as high-value AI-infrastructure networking evidence instead of canonical strong.

historical_watchlist.title: EnvPilot: Systematic Design and Evaluation of an Experience-Augmented Agent for Software Environment Setup
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / software engineering agents / trajectory memory / experience reuse
historical_watchlist.why: Maintains a trajectory-derived memory initialized with 667 validated experiences and retrieves prior setup strategies to avoid redundant exploration. On 112 real GitHub instances across nine languages it reaches 75% Pass@1 while the paper reports reduced reasoning cost, but the primary abstract does not expose a clean quantitative token/latency/cost reduction, so it remains a high-value watch item.

historical_watchlist.title: Beyond Fluent Generation: A CPU Reliability Benchmark for MCP-Style Tool Calling in Sub-2B Small Language Models for Edge Deployment
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / tool-using SLMs / CPU inference / reliability-resource tradeoff
historical_watchlist.why: Provides an explicit edge-agent resource baseline for sub-2B tool-calling models. Qwen2.5-1.5B uses 7,960 MiB and 30.782 s mean CPU latency versus 3,637 MiB and 10.627 s for Qwen2.5-0.5B, while reliability changes substantially. This is valuable deployment evidence but a benchmark rather than a new acceleration method, so it stays watch.

historical_watchlist.title: OmniNav: Robust Long-Horizon Target Navigation in Dynamic Environments
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / long-horizon navigation / persistent scene memory / closed-loop recovery
historical_watchlist.why: Maintains an updatable 3D object scene memory, revises target beliefs under partial observability, and propagates execution feedback through hierarchical closed-loop recovery. It improves real-world pick-and-place success from 53.3% to 71.7% over an adapted open-loop baseline. This is strong protected evidence for persistent embodied memory and closed-loop execution, but it does not claim inference acceleration.

historical_watchlist.title: Drive by Hindsight and Foresight: Tool-Grounded Synergistic Reasoning over Hierarchical Memory for Autonomous Driving
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / autonomous driving / hierarchical memory / proactive tool invocation
historical_watchlist.why: Couples scene-level short-term memory, evolving long-term experience memory and adaptive tool invocation in a closed reasoning loop. Its 7B model reaches 79.09% MCQ on DriveLMM-o1, with short-term memory improving STSBench by 24.2 points and frozen-parameter long-term memory adding 3.57 MCQ points. It is valuable Physical-AI memory/tool-use evidence, but the reported contribution is capability rather than inference efficiency.

historical_watchlist.title: IBIB: A Protocol for Measuring Enterprise AI Systems by Serving Route, Not Model Identifier
historical_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / deployment measurement / serving route / precision and harness
historical_watchlist.why: Measures enterprise AI systems at the actual serving-route level rather than advertised model identifier, explicitly binding weights, precision, output contract and harness. The reference protocol covers 128 tasks and 987 assertions and treats route failures as deployment evidence. High-value systems measurement work, but not a new acceleration method.

historical_watchlist.title: Towards Scalable and Cost-Efficient Vulnerability Detection: A Study on Automatic Query Generation
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / code agents / cost-efficient static analysis
historical_watchlist.why: Uses LLMs to synthesize reusable CodeQL queries instead of repeatedly scanning repositories with full LLM reasoning; reports 82% average F1 improvement over baseline CodeQL and includes a cost-benefit analysis showing direct full-repository LLM scanning can be computationally and financially expensive. Retained as high-value agentic tooling watch rather than acceleration strong.

historical_watchlist.title: Fortunate Recall: Ontology-Driven Memory Lifecycle Management for Persistent Coherence in LLMs
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / persistent memory / lifecycle management
historical_watchlist.why: Introduces typed memory lifecycle policies for persistent LLM agents. FR-Bank reaches 76.9% on LifecycleBench and 75.2% on LongMemEval-S while avoiding unbounded undifferentiated memory growth; useful agent-memory infrastructure evidence, but no direct latency/throughput reduction is established in the primary abstract.

historical_watchlist.title: JarvisGUI: Towards Cross-Device GUI Agents with Dynamic Task Composition
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / GUI agents / heterogeneous devices / state transfer
historical_watchlist.why: Benchmarks cross-device GUI workflows across Android, Windows and Ubuntu using typed input-output composition and exposes state-transfer and long-horizon coordination failures. Important heterogeneous-agent infrastructure benchmark, but it does not claim a measured inference acceleration method.

historical_watchlist.title: UnitBoost: Managing Compound LLM Systems with a Merge Operator, Not a Model
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / compound LLM systems / non-generative orchestration
historical_watchlist.why: Replaces the generative meta-agent manager with an order-free merge operator and explicit residual-directed rounds, improving multiple compound-system configurations and removing a higher-level generative coordination step. It is highly relevant to agent serving efficiency, but the primary abstract does not provide a clean latency/token/cost reduction figure, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Testing Interchangeability in LLM Agent Teams
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / multi-agent communication / coordination cost
historical_watchlist.why: Shows that swapping role-matched agents can preserve task score while increasing communication per unit progress by 16-63%, with larger penalties after longer team formation. This is useful systems characterization of hidden multi-agent coordination cost, but not an acceleration method.

historical_watchlist.title: JEPA Policy: Diffusion-Free Imitation Learning via Paired Action and Future Representation Prediction
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / diffusion-free action policy / low-latency visuomotor imitation
historical_watchlist.why: Uses paired action and future-representation prediction instead of iterative diffusion sampling. Across nine simulated tasks it improves over MIP and outperforms Diffusion Policy under evaluated settings while adding only 0.29 ms to MIP model latency; a five-task 630-episode real-robot study preserves the ranking. Strong protected Physical-AI signal, but the primary abstract does not quantify speedup versus Diffusion Policy, so retained as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Router Prior Bias: Preserving Base Routing Structure in MoE Post-Training
historical_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / router post-training / expert co-activation
historical_watchlist.why: Shows downstream MoE post-training benefits from softly preserving the pretrained router prior rather than re-imposing uniform load balancing. Important expert-routing lineage on Moonlight-16B-A3B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, but no measured serving throughput/latency gain in the primary abstract.

historical_watchlist.title: Beyond Scalar Flexibility: From Eligible AI Workloads to Dependable Load Relief
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / datacenter power / workload flexibility
historical_watchlist.why: Reconstructs 4,439 hourly power observations from a 185-day trace of 155,410 GPUs and derives duration/reliability-aware AI workload flexibility. Valuable production-scale AI-infrastructure power characterization, but not an ML acceleration technique.

historical_watchlist.title: Closing the Consistency Gap: Self-Evolving Agents That Learn to Stay on Course
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / episodic memory / production consistency
historical_watchlist.why: Converts unstable agent trajectory steps into episodic guidelines. On AppWorld with ReAct/GPT-4.1, all-five-runs success improves by +16 points same-task and +13 points similar-task. High-value agent-runtime reliability work, but not direct inference acceleration.

historical_watchlist.title: Linear Algebra Foundations of Efficient Attention: A Phase Reversal in Rank Collapse Under SVD Compression
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / low-rank compression / KV-cache lineage
historical_watchlist.why: Unifies low-rank attention/KV-cache compression literature and adds a controlled finding that SVD compression reverses its rank-collapse behavior between initialization and pretrained models. Useful compression-mechanism lineage, but it does not present a direct serving latency/throughput improvement, so it stays watchlist.

historical_watchlist.title: One Word, Different Action: A Real-Robot Benchmark for Language-Conditioned Embodied Reasoning
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / real-robot benchmark / language-conditioned action reasoning
historical_watchlist.why: Introduces a real-robot benchmark that separates decision invariance from decision sensitivity under minimal instruction changes, multi-constraint reasoning, and real-RGB grounding. It exposes failures when multiple constraints must be composed into one executable action, making it useful protected Physical-AI coverage, but it is a benchmark rather than an inference-efficiency method.

historical_watchlist.title: Privacy-Preserving Split Learning for Federated LLM Fine-Tuning
historical_watchlist.topic: distributed training/inference / federated LLM fine-tuning / split learning privacy
historical_watchlist.why: Partitions LLM fine-tuning across resource-constrained clients and a server, then adds learned obfuscate-and-recover protection against autoregressive activation leakage. The paper reports strong privacy with modest utility loss and system overhead; relevant to heterogeneous/federated LLM systems, but the primary source does not establish a strong acceleration win.

historical_watchlist.title: CreaMem: A Scene-Aware Memory Architecture for Personalized Agents
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / long-term memory / retrieval organization
historical_watchlist.why: Partitions long-term agent memory by life scene and dual-codes memories from episodic and trait perspectives, directly targeting retrieval-space inflation and cross-scene interference. It is useful lineage for efficient agent memory organization, but the primary abstract does not establish a clean latency/token-cost reduction, so it remains high-value watchlist.

historical_watchlist.title: Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / procedural memory / long-horizon tool use
historical_watchlist.why: Externalizes procedural knowledge into a self-evolving graph and localizes the active procedure node before each action, addressing repeated or out-of-order tool calls in long trajectories. Strong runtime-structure relevance, but the abstract does not provide a clean serving-cost or latency gain, so it remains watchlist.

historical_watchlist.title: La Agente Óptima: Towards Agentic Self-Driving Laboratories
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / autonomous experimentation / conditional agent invocation
historical_watchlist.why: Separates LLM reasoning from persistent Bayesian-optimization campaigns: repetitive closed-loop optimization proceeds without repeatedly invoking the agent, and control returns to the LLM only when interpretation or campaign revision is needed. This conditional-invocation pattern is relevant to Physical-AI runtime design, but no clean inference-speedup metric is given in the abstract.

historical_watchlist.title: One Shared LoRA Weight for MRI Reconstruction across Acceleration Factors
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient training/inference / parameter-efficient adaptation / shared LoRA
historical_watchlist.why: Uses one shared LoRA adapter set plus a lightweight gate across multiple acceleration factors instead of maintaining separate models, with trainable parameters reported at only about 5% of the backbone while retaining competitive reconstruction quality. Useful parameter/storage-efficiency evidence, but domain-specific and without a direct serving speedup claim.

historical_watchlist.title: WIP: Energy-Efficient LLM-Based Serving Cluster Formulation in Cell-Free Massive MIMO
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / LLM agent resource control / wireless energy efficiency
historical_watchlist.why: Uses an LLM-based agent to formulate serving clusters in a simulated cell-free massive-MIMO network and reports up to 32% energy-efficiency gain over the baseline. Relevant to AI-native edge/network resource control, but it is a work-in-progress networking application rather than core ML serving infrastructure, so it remains watchlist.

historical_watchlist.title: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models: On-Policy Correction Helps Weaker Models Catch Up Where Imitation Fails
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / harness optimization / small-model deployment
historical_watchlist.why: Studies co-evolution of agent harnesses and lightweight model adaptation across seven enterprise tasks. Evolved harnesses let weaker models approach stronger-model behavior at lower deployment cost, while naive expert-trajectory imitation can regress 4-30 points. Strong evidence that runtime scaffolding and model adaptation must be co-designed, but the abstract does not provide a clean latency/token-cost reduction, so it remains high-value watchlist.

historical_watchlist.title: Benchmarking Agentic HLS Design Tasks With HLS-Eval
historical_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / hardware design automation / agent cost profiling
historical_watchlist.why: Extends HLS-Eval with an agentic flow that edits code, compiles for self-verification, iterates during inference, and logs cost, token usage, and iteration count. Highly relevant to AI-for-hardware workflow efficiency and tool-use evaluation, but it is primarily a benchmark rather than a demonstrated acceleration method.

historical_watchlist.title: Storage-Scalable Progressive Semantic Communication via Knowledge-Base Reuse
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / semantic communication / storage efficiency
historical_watchlist.why: Reuses a compact set of knowledge bases across progressive residual refinement stages, decoupling maintained-KB storage from transmission depth while preserving competitive semantic reconstruction. Useful edge/communication storage-efficiency evidence, but the abstract does not give a clean end-to-end AI serving latency or energy gain.

historical_watchlist.title: Human-Human & Human-Robot Interaction Transformer (H2INT) for Robot Navigation in Dense and Uncertain Crowds
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot navigation / interaction modeling
historical_watchlist.why: Uses a gated Transformer and recurrent policy to model human-human and human-robot interactions under heterogeneous pedestrian responsiveness. It is a useful Physical-AI navigation and temporal-interaction lineage point, but it does not establish inference acceleration or deployment-efficiency gains in the primary abstract.

historical_watchlist.title: Where to Look and What to Use: Retrieve-Localize-Generate for Long-Term Conversational Memory Question Answering
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / long-term memory / retrieval localization
historical_watchlist.why: Introduces MemLoc, combining multi-granularity memory retrieval, graph-based cross-session routing, and a reasoning-based evidence localizer to reduce noisy long-context evidence before generation. The architecture is directly relevant to efficient long-term agent memory, but the primary abstract does not provide a clean token/latency reduction, so it remains watchlist.

historical_watchlist.title: Do Agents Know When They Succeed? Calibrating Agent Confidence from Internal Representations
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / runtime reliability / confidence monitoring
historical_watchlist.why: Uses residual-stream trajectory dynamics and action-representation probes to predict eventual agent success across Bash, SQL, and Python tasks and three model families. It reports a zero-overhead reliability monitor requiring neither prompt changes nor multi-sample rollouts; highly relevant to low-cost agent runtime control, but the abstract does not quantify end-to-end serving savings.

historical_watchlist.title: BEFORE THE FLIP: Measuring Hidden Score Shifts In Quantized Vision Language Models Before The Answer Changes for Visual Question Answering
historical_watchlist.why: Shows that 4-bit compression can materially shift VLM answer margins even when discrete answers remain unchanged, while per-question mixed-precision selection fails to beat shuffled controls at tested storage budgets. Useful evidence that VLM quantization evaluation should inspect hidden score movement rather than answer flips alone, but it does not introduce a new acceleration method.

historical_watchlist.title: PlayTrain: An Efficient Reinforcement Learning Framework for LLM-Generated Adaptable JavaScript Games
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / RL infrastructure / simulation throughput
historical_watchlist.why: Combines LLM-generated JavaScript environments with a high-throughput RL pipeline and reports over 1M agent decisions per second on a single GPU node. This is strong infrastructure evidence for cheap scalable agent-environment generation and training, but it is not directly an LLM serving or inference acceleration method.

historical_watchlist.title: DISEIL: Demonstration Distillation for Sample-Efficient Imitation Learning
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / imitation learning / data efficiency
historical_watchlist.why: Clusters recurring robot-policy failure modes and asks for targeted demonstrations starting at the first unreliable step. Across five simulated tasks and both state/image observations it achieves the highest mean held-out success in all ten settings, with the largest margin at the smallest demonstration budget. Important Physical-AI data-efficiency evidence, though not inference acceleration.

historical_watchlist.title: IM-ENGINE: Image Editing for Embodied Data Generation
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / embodied data generation / simulation
historical_watchlist.why: Uses image editing as an intermediate representation, then recovers simulator-grounded 3D state and physics-valid robot supervision for grasping and goal-state generation. It offers a scalable alternative to costly human demonstrations and is relevant to embodied training-data efficiency, but the primary abstract provides no direct runtime acceleration metric.

historical_watchlist.title: Eliciting Self-Verification in Multimodal Reasoning Agents with Reinforcement Learning
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / multimodal tool use / self-verification
historical_watchlist.why: SVRL trains multimodal agents to verify and filter retrieved evidence internally, adds a search-aware penalty against unnecessary tool calls, and reports consistent gains in tool efficiency while narrowing the gap between compact open models and much larger proprietary systems with substantially lower training and inference cost. The primary abstract does not provide a clean end-to-end latency or cost ratio, so it remains high-value watch rather than strong.

historical_watchlist.title: From Narrative to Auditable Forecasts: A Structured Scaffold for Agentic Forecasting
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / adaptive scaffold / cost-aware inference
historical_watchlist.why: AuditForecast replaces unstructured narrative aggregation with a quantitative baseline, targeted retrieval and mechanical odds-space updates. Across live forecasting benchmarks it improves accuracy/calibration and outperforms substantially more expensive deep-research agents while remaining Pareto-dominant in the cost-accuracy tradeoff. Useful agent-system evidence, but the abstract does not expose a single reproducible latency or dollar-cost reduction ratio.

historical_watchlist.title: What Should an Agent Forget? Separating What Is Stored from What Is Used
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / long-term memory / context compression
historical_watchlist.why: RD-Forget separates a persistent source archive from a query-conditioned answer-time memory view and uses a rate-distortion formulation to construct that view under an explicit memory budget. It directly targets the long-context inefficiency of retaining everything in the prompt while preserving historical access, making it relevant to agent memory serving, though the abstract does not quantify wall-clock or token savings.

historical_watchlist.title: RoboDrop: Curating VLA Post-Training Data via Local Gradient Compatibility
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / post-training data efficiency / data curation
historical_watchlist.why: RoboDrop scores robot demonstrations online during a one-epoch warm-up using local gradient compatibility against task-semantic and visually matched validation samples, then filters harmful episodes automatically. It targets the high cost and brittleness of VLA post-training data collection across controlled corruptions, simulation and real-robot datasets. This is protected Physical-AI data-efficiency work rather than an inference accelerator.

historical_watchlist.title: OmniEye: Efficient Multimodal Forensic Video Intelligence for Law-Enforcement Body-Worn Cameras
historical_watchlist.why: OmniEye processes 30-second audiovisual windows with a multimodal foundation model, stores structured outputs in SQLite/BM25, and re-perceives only retrieved candidate windows for grounded questioning. The complete system is reported to run on a single 16 GB GPU using a 4-bit quantization-aware-trained model, giving useful deployment evidence for retrieval-gated multimodal serving, but without a direct speedup baseline.

historical_watchlist.title: Large Language Models with At Most One Spike per Neuron
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / energy-efficient LLM / spiking inference
historical_watchlist.why: A fully time-to-first-spike LLM formulation is scaled to 1.5B parameters and reports extremely sparse event-driven activity with an energy estimate from spike counts. Because the paper explicitly notes this is a proxy under a cost model rather than measurement on neuromorphic hardware, it is preserved as high-value watch rather than promoted strong.

historical_watchlist.title: FrogNano: Training a 4B Coding Agent via Online Task Synthesis
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / small coding agents / resource-constrained deployment
historical_watchlist.why: FrogNano trains a 4B coding agent with online task synthesis and reinforcement learning on about 1,500 SWE environments, targeting capable coding agents that can operate under minimal hardware budgets. It is relevant to efficient-agent deployment, but the abstract does not expose a clean latency, memory, or serving-cost reduction ratio.

historical_watchlist.title: Unified Vision-Centric Pedestrian Crossing Action Prediction via Adaptive Patch Projection and Proactive Spatial Rectification
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / multimodal token efficiency / autonomous driving
historical_watchlist.why: ViCross targets the cost of high-resolution full-frame MLLM encoding with variable-resolution patch mapping that allocates visual tokens adaptively around pedestrians while preserving target-centric reasoning. This is protected Physical-AI token-efficiency work, but the primary abstract does not provide a reproducible wall-clock or token-reduction ratio.

historical_watchlist.title: From Deep to Shallow: Unconstrained and Efficient Layer Merging Strategy
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / model compression / embedded inference
historical_watchlist.why: The method merges redundant layers without requiring an analytical merge rule and avoids the kernel-size growth that can erase practical speedups. The authors report inference speed-up measurements on real embedded platforms across architectures and datasets, making it relevant deployment evidence, but the abstract omits a clean numerical speedup ratio.

historical_watchlist.title: SCAPES: Semantically Conditioned Autoregressive Prior for Environmental Sounds
historical_watchlist.topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / lightweight generative models / single-GPU training
historical_watchlist.why: SCAPES uses a 36M-parameter latent continuous-normalizing-flow model with flow matching and reports training on a single consumer GPU with convergence after roughly twice the source-audio duration. It is useful evidence for lightweight generative modeling, but it is not yet a direct image/video serving accelerator and lacks an end-to-end baseline speedup.

historical_watchlist.title: GRACE: Graph-Grounded Reflective Agent Copilot Engine for Expert-in-the-Loop Knowledge Expansion
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / cost-aware verification / RAG agents
historical_watchlist.why: GRACE uses a Return-on-Attention objective to defer uncertain claims to expert or agent review only when priority-weighted uncertainty justifies verification cost. This is relevant adaptive-compute evidence for agentic RAG, but lacks a clean latency or dollar-cost reduction ratio.

historical_watchlist.title: ICM-Bench: Person-Level Identity Reasoning in Multimodal Agents with Long-Term Memory
historical_watchlist.why: ICM-Bench isolates identity-centric long-term memory over 839 synthetic clips and 1,217 questions and compares caption-memory, memory-augmented agents and graph retrieval. It is a useful memory-system evaluation node, but primarily a benchmark rather than an efficiency method.

historical_watchlist.title: $τ^τ$-Bench: An Environment for End-To-End, Realistic Agent Construction
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / serving-cost benchmark / agent construction
historical_watchlist.why: $τ^τ$-Bench makes serving cost and model choice part of end-to-end agent construction across 53 realistic tasks and evaluates deployed agents against held-out users. It is useful infrastructure evidence for cost-aware agent engineering, but is a benchmark rather than an acceleration method.

historical_watchlist.title: DAREBench: Deployment-Aware and Reliable Evaluation of Models as Agents
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / deployment benchmark / cost-aware model selection
historical_watchlist.why: DAREBench evaluates 35 commercial and local models over 7,587 agent runs and reports accuracy, token consumption and API reference cost across a workload matrix. It is valuable for deployment-aware agent quality-cost selection, but is primarily a benchmark rather than an acceleration method.

historical_watchlist.title: PRAGMA: Evaluating Personalized Guidance with Memory Alignment in Lifelong Conversations
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / long-term memory / retrieval benchmark
historical_watchlist.why: PRAGMA targets the computational and reliability problems of full conversational histories and evaluates retrieval, memory and long-context systems for personalized guidance. It is a useful long-term-memory systems benchmark, but the abstract does not quantify end-to-end token or latency savings.

historical_watchlist.title: PhysMAS: Physics-Grounded Multi-Agent Synthesis of Compositional 4D Gaussians
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / 4D Gaussian world modeling / physics agents
historical_watchlist.why: PhysMAS uses persistent object-part identity, material reasoning agents and solver-aware skills for physically executable 4D Gaussian synthesis, explicitly avoiding SDS-style repeated score evaluations and backpropagation. It is protected Physical-AI evidence, but the abstract lacks a clean runtime or memory ratio.

historical_watchlist.title: Adaptive Gated Deepfake Detection for Low-Resolution and Resource-Constrained Environments
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / adaptive inference / early exit
historical_watchlist.why: AdaGate-DF routes samples through a dual multi-exit path using image-quality cues so easier inputs can exit early, targeting resource-constrained inference while maintaining competitive detection accuracy. The abstract reports low latency but no clean speedup ratio, so it remains a watch item.

historical_watchlist.title: VLX-VR: An Agentic-Aware Video Reasoning Model
historical_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / adaptive evidence acquisition / agent memory
historical_watchlist.why: VLX-VR uses a Think-Memory-Observation loop so a video reasoning model can adaptively acquire evidence, read or write memory, and decide when to terminate rather than relying on fixed-context single-pass processing. It is relevant to adaptive multimodal serving, but the abstract provides quality rather than latency or token-cost measurements.

historical_watchlist.title: Dynamic Adaptation of the LLM Context for Generating Routines with Coupled Semantics
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / dynamic context / sample-efficient search
historical_watchlist.why: A validation agent converts execution traces into structured diagnostics that dynamically adapt generation context, outperforming Reflexion and OpenEvolve at matched 300-600 evaluation budgets on most tested problems. This is useful sample-efficiency evidence for agentic code search, but not a direct serving accelerator.

historical_watchlist.title: Agentic AI-enabled Semantic Commissioning of a Cognitive Digital Twin for Reconfigurable Manufacturing
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / industrial agents / runtime orchestration
historical_watchlist.why: A LangGraph multi-agent workflow combines RAG and MCP-based telemetry binding for a robotic machining cell and reports reducing commissioning from several weeks to about two hours. It is strong workflow-efficiency evidence for industrial Physical AI, but the gain is deployment-process automation rather than model inference acceleration.

historical_watchlist.title: Mathematical Modeling of a Cognitive Continuum Digital Shadow for Large-Scale, Cross-Facility Workflows
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / cross-facility scheduling / cost-energy optimization
historical_watchlist.why: The Cognitive Continuum Digital Shadow models cross-facility instruments, networks, storage and compute with stochastic optimization to expose cost, makespan and energy trade-offs before execution. It is relevant heterogeneous-infrastructure scheduling evidence, but this first paper is primarily a mathematical formulation rather than measured AI-serving acceleration.

historical_watchlist.title: Signed Rescue Routing: Harm-Aware Cascades for Efficient LLM Inference
historical_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / model routing / adaptive compute
historical_watchlist.why: SRR routes requests between Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B by predicting signed incremental gain rather than uncertainty. The method is directly about budgeted efficient inference and uses a lightweight deployment router, but the current abstract still contains TBD quantitative results, so it is retained as high-value watch rather than promoted strong.

historical_watchlist.title: Matryoshka Hash Representations for Model-Aware Compact Semantic Retrieval
historical_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / RAG retrieval / compact index
historical_watchlist.why: MHR stores documents at one bit per coordinate while supporting directly searchable prefixes at multiple byte budgets and FAISS FastScan. It directly attacks corpus-scale dense-index storage and preserves strong retrieval quality, but does not report end-to-end RAG serving latency.

historical_watchlist.title: FreeTransformSR: Efficient Lightweight Image Super-Resolution via Free Low-Rank Learnable Transform
historical_watchlist.topic: video/image generation acceleration / lightweight image restoration
historical_watchlist.why: FreeTransformSR reports 595K parameters, significantly fewer FLOPs, and faster inference than competing super-resolution methods while preserving competitive quality. It is useful lightweight vision-generation evidence, but the abstract lacks a clean common-platform speedup ratio.

historical_watchlist.title: A Brain-inspired Hierarchical Framework for Zero-Shot Robot Task Reasoning and Execution
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / hierarchical robot reasoning / closed-loop execution
historical_watchlist.why: The framework decomposes robot reasoning into perception/state inference, language grounding, reusable atomic actions, cost-based plan selection, and refreshed-observation verification, outperforming ReKep, Dream2Flow and pi0.5 on tested tasks. It is valuable Physical-AI system lineage but provides no measured inference/runtime efficiency.

historical_watchlist.title: No Free Checker: A Survey of Verifiers for Robot Policies
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / policy verification / runtime monitors
historical_watchlist.why: This survey organizes roughly 150 robot-policy verifiers around availability (cost, latency, density) and credibility, directly exposing the runtime cost-versus-trust tradeoff for VLA policy checking. It is a protected Physical-AI reference rather than an acceleration method.

historical_watchlist.title: Observe Before You Alert: Adaptive Driver Alerting with Vision-Language Models
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / adaptive perception / driver alerting
historical_watchlist.why: VLAlert introduces SILENT/OBSERVE/ALERT actions so a VLM can delay uncertain warnings and adapt the next observation window. It is relevant to adaptive Physical-AI perception and runtime control, but reports decision quality rather than inference speed or compute reduction.

historical_watchlist.title: JEDI: JEPA-to-Edge Distillation for Efficient Cropland Segmentation from Satellite Imagery
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / distillation / compact vision
historical_watchlist.why: JEDI distills a 639M-parameter I-JEPA teacher into compact 4.04M-28M SegFormer students while preserving much of the task quality. The compression ratio is substantial and deployment-motivated, but the application is remote sensing and the abstract lacks direct latency/energy measurements.

historical_watchlist.title: LLM-Aided Design for Manufacturing: A Multi-Agent System for Intent-Preserving Redesign of CAD for Improved Manufacturability
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / industrial agents / tool-using verification
historical_watchlist.why: A multimodal-LLM reviewer and CAD-modifier agent iteratively propose, compile, visually verify and revise manufacturing-oriented CAD edits. It is useful lineage for tool-using industrial Physical-AI agents, but the contribution is task robustness rather than inference efficiency.

historical_watchlist.title: ReCAST: Restoration-aware Cascaded Stage-wise Training for Obfuscated SMS Risk Classification
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / distillation / deployable small models
historical_watchlist.why: ReCAST distills a large teacher de-obfuscation capability into a smaller deployable student under production-oriented latency and throughput constraints. It is relevant to compact production inference, but the abstract does not provide concrete speedup, memory, or cost numbers.

historical_watchlist.title: Monkey See, Can Monkey Do? A Benchmark for Evaluating Robot Skill Learning by Observation
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot learning / data scaling benchmark
historical_watchlist.why: RoboReel provides a unified benchmark for learning robot policies from human videos across ten manipulation tasks and seven-plus algorithms including VLA variants. It directly addresses robotics data scaling and long-horizon robustness, but is a benchmark rather than an inference accelerator.

historical_watchlist.title: What Matters, When? Diagnosing and Improving Conditional Visual Grounding in Visuomotor Imitation Policies
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / visuomotor grounding / robustness
historical_watchlist.why: Systematically localizes distractor failures to phase-conditional target selection in ACT and a pretrained VLA policy, then tests augmentation, attention regularization and visual prompting on simulation and a physical UR3e. It is useful Physical-AI runtime/robustness lineage, but does not report inference speed or compute reduction.

historical_watchlist.title: Improving 5G AI-RAN MCS Selection by Predicting Retransmissions
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / AI-RAN / low-latency inference
historical_watchlist.why: NOSTRAdAMUS deploys a predictive link-adaptation dApp with 5.5 microsecond inference latency and reports up to 71.5% goodput improvement and 71.8% retransmission reduction on real and hardware-in-the-loop 5G setups. It is strong edge-runtime evidence, though the workload is network control rather than AI-model serving itself.

historical_watchlist.title: PAI-Actor: Cinematic Multi-Character Replacement in Dynamic Scenes
historical_watchlist.topic: video/image generation acceleration / autoregressive distillation / long-form generation
historical_watchlist.why: PAI-Actor distills a high-quality bidirectional diffusion transformer into an autoregressive video-to-video model for more efficient long-form 1080P generation. The systems direction is directly relevant, but the abstract does not provide concrete latency, throughput, or FLOP reductions.

historical_watchlist.title: MOAE: Multi-Objective Agent Evolution with Pareto-Preserving Search
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / rollout-budget optimization / Pareto search
historical_watchlist.why: MOAE performs parameter-free in-context agent evolution while preserving non-dominated rollouts under a limited rollout budget, explicitly including efficiency among deployment objectives. It is relevant to cost-aware agent construction, but the abstract lacks direct token/API/latency savings.

historical_watchlist.title: RealSimLoop: Online Real-to-Sim Adaptation via Differentiable Reduced-Order Simulation with Vision Feedback
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / differentiable simulation / online adaptation
historical_watchlist.why: RealSimLoop runs differentiable simulation in a reduced-order neural subspace and couples it with differentiable rendering for online vision-feedback parameter adaptation, reporting quasi-real-time operation and downstream force/stress estimation. This is directly relevant to efficient Physical-AI world-model/runtime loops, but the abstract lacks a clean speedup ratio or latency number.

historical_watchlist.title: MetroLLM-Bench: Evaluating Language Models as Transit Kiosk Runtimes
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / compact agent runtime / PEFT
historical_watchlist.why: MetroLLM-Bench shows a PEFT-trained Qwen 3.5 4B student with a 2.6 GB Q4_K_M footprint matching or exceeding much larger frontier models on deterministic kiosk-policy scoring, while larger 9B/27B students bring no Tier-1 gain. It is strong compact-agent deployment evidence, but the paper is primarily a benchmark and does not report end-to-end serving latency or cost.

historical_watchlist.title: SharedSAE: One Feature Dictionary Across Language Models
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / interpretability infrastructure / shared representation
historical_watchlist.why: SharedSAE replaces separate per-model sparse-autoencoder dictionaries with one shared dictionary plus model-specific encoder-decoder pairs; it retains 96.6% of dedicated-SAE explained variance and allows efficient adaptation of new models while reusing labels. This materially reduces duplicated interpretability infrastructure, though it is not inference-serving acceleration.

historical_watchlist.title: ARC-Loc: Leveraging Azimuthal Ray Convergence as a Geometric Cue for Direct Cross-View Localization
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / geometric localization / lightweight perception
historical_watchlist.why: ARC-Loc removes computationally heavy BEV transforms and external depth-foundation-model dependencies by direct ground-to-satellite geometric matching, reporting faster and more memory-efficient inference while keeping competitive localization accuracy. It is relevant to edge Physical-AI perception, but the abstract omits concrete latency/memory ratios.

historical_watchlist.title: MEOX: Compact Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts for Earth Observation
historical_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / compact multimodal MoE / parameter efficiency
historical_watchlist.why: MEOX combines modality adapters, validity signals, sparse experts, low-rank residuals, and rotary attention in a 2.939M-parameter encoder while achieving strong frozen-transfer results. The workload is Earth observation, but the architecture is a useful compact multimodal-MoE efficiency datapoint; no direct serving latency or energy result is given.

historical_watchlist.title: Scal3R: Learning Efficient Multi-Relative Pose Query for Scalable Online 3D Reconstruction
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / online 3D reconstruction / lightweight pose queries
historical_watchlist.why: Scal3R keeps the reconstruction backbone frozen and adds lightweight multi-reference pose-query tokens amounting to about 1% of parameters to stabilize long-video online 3D reconstruction. It is a strong lightweight Physical-AI perception idea, but the abstract does not provide a clean wall-clock or memory reduction ratio.

historical_watchlist.title: Beyond Similarity: Foundation Models as an Efficient Backbone for Training-Free Composed Video Retrieval
historical_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / adaptive inference depth / video retrieval
historical_watchlist.why: The framework uses reusable compact gallery embeddings first, then bounded reranking, candidate expansion, target-description generation and multimodal verification only for increasingly ambiguous cases. This is a useful adaptive-compute serving pattern for video retrieval, but the abstract emphasizes retrieval accuracy rather than measured latency or cost savings.

historical_watchlist.title: Neuron-Guided Fine-Tuning: Unlocking Efficient Alignment Mechanisms for Large Language Models
historical_watchlist.topic: quantization/sparsity/pruning / parameter-efficient LLM fine-tuning / activation-guided updates
historical_watchlist.why: NGFT uses activation patterns to select task-relevant neurons in one forward pass, select information-dense data, and align activations to pretrained states, explicitly targeting parameter redundancy and fine-tuning efficiency. The abstract claims efficiency gains but gives no concrete compute, memory or wall-clock ratio, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Phase-and-First-Arrival VLM Feedback for Sparse-Reward Reinforcement Learning in Surgical Manipulation
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot learning / sparse VLM supervision
historical_watchlist.why: The method uses one VLM query per recorded robot episode to identify the furthest verified task phase and its first arrival time, reusing partial progress for sparse-reward learning. It is valuable Physical-AI supervision-efficiency evidence, but the paper primarily improves learning signal quality rather than inference runtime.

historical_watchlist.title: RiLM: Parameter-Efficient Language Modeling via Geodesic Decoding
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / compact language models / parameter efficiency
historical_watchlist.why: RiLM removes the conventional output projection by sharing the token embedding geometry for input and geodesic decoding, targeting sub-million-parameter language models for edge deployment. The controlled results are interesting parameter-efficiency evidence, but the work is small-model focused and lacks wall-clock or energy measurements.

historical_watchlist.title: TROVE: Adaptive Agent Skill Orchestration via Trace-Grounded Route Validation and Editing
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / adaptive orchestration / compute avoidance
historical_watchlist.why: TROVE preserves valid workflow fragments and revises only execution steps invalidated by new runtime evidence, explicitly targeting wasted computation from stale plans and broad replanning. This is a useful agent-runtime adaptive-compute pattern, but the abstract does not provide a clean latency/token/cost reduction ratio.

historical_watchlist.title: Design Docs Are All You Need: An AI-native Machine-Learning Performance Tool
historical_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / ML performance modeling / agentic tooling
historical_watchlist.why: SMART stores a DAG of design documents and uses coding agents to regenerate an ML-system performance-modeling library as hardware/model assumptions change. It is relevant AI-infra tooling for rapidly evolving accelerator/software stacks, but it is a performance-modeling workflow rather than a direct inference/training acceleration method.

historical_watchlist.title: Cross-Domain Tracker Adaptation Without Target-Domain Labels via Vision-Language Agents
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / vision-language agents / online perception adaptation
historical_watchlist.why: A VLM diagnostic agent inspects tracking failures and iteratively adjusts a detect-to-track pipeline without target-domain labels, recovering a substantial fraction of oracle adaptation performance.
